burdens.description: Executive support depends on recovering the right context at the right moment—without turning every meeting, decision, and follow-up into another manual chase.

items.label: Context

items.description: Agenda changes, late documents, earlier decisions, and attendee context often converge only hours before the meeting.

items.label: Format
items.title: Decisions vanish into notes
items.description: A decision may be clear in the room but later disappear among transcripts, personal notes, and unconfirmed interpretations.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Follow-ups cross too many channels

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Leaders need summaries at different depths
items.description: The same week may need a two-minute overview, a decision brief, and a detailed source trail for different audiences.

workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for an executive-support Work Agent
workflows.title: Delegate meeting preparation and follow-through without delegating authority.
workflows.description: Each assignment starts from approved context, produces an inspectable brief or draft, and stops before commitments, sensitive distribution, or executive decisions.

items.title: Prepare an executive meeting brief

items.output: A concise brief with agenda, background, and decision points.

items.title: Turn a meeting into accountable follow-up

boundaries.retainsTitle: executive assistants and operations partners retain

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not an executive proxy. Its workspace keeps approved context, tools, instructions, and drafts together; assistants and leaders retain control of confidential access, commitments, recipients, and final decisions.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for executive assistants and operations partners
faq.description: Executive assistants need speed without losing discretion, recipient awareness, decision ownership, or control over sensitive organizational context.

items.question: Is Floatboat an executive calendar or task-management system?
items.answer: No. Calendars and task systems remain the records of commitments. Floatboat helps assemble meeting context, draft briefs, recover decisions, and prepare updates across those sources.

items.question: Can it decide priorities or commit an executive's time?
items.answer: It can surface conflicts and prepare options, but the executive and authorized staff decide priorities, access, delegation, and calendar commitments.

items.question: Can it follow an executive's preferred briefing format?
items.answer: Yes. Define the expected length, sections, decision framing, confidentiality labels, source links, and what should be omitted for each audience.

items.question: How do we prevent an uncertain note from becoming a recorded decision?
items.answer: Keep proposed, discussed, and confirmed decisions separate; link entries to the meeting source; and require the responsible person to confirm ownership, wording, and due dates.

items.question: How should board, personnel, or deal context be handled?
items.answer: Follow organizational classification and need-to-know rules, isolate sensitive work where needed, and verify the processing behavior and permissions of each connected model and tool.

items.question: Can it send follow-ups or place events directly on calendars?
items.answer: It can prepare messages and proposed calendar actions, but an authorized person should confirm the recipient, commitment, timing, and visibility before execution.

items.question: What is a useful first executive-support workflow?
items.answer: Use one recurring leadership meeting. Assemble the agenda, previous decisions, current documents, and open actions into a brief, then verify it with the executive before saving the pattern.

finalCta.title: Walk into the meeting with the brief prepared
finalCta.description: Use the agenda and real source material to prepare a reviewable brief. People still decide what to promise and what to send.
